media:group.media:description:

entry.title: Quantum chaos and simple equations with Prof Jens Marklof - Episode #76

author.name: Isaac Newton Institute for Mathematical Sciences

media:group.media:title: Quantum chaos and simple equations with Prof Jens Marklof - Episode #76
media:group.media:description:
Send us Fan Mail (https://www.buzzsprout.com/1992011/fan_mail/new)
A chaotic system is one where the outcome is sensitively dependent on initial conditions. Small disturbances can take the system in new, unpredictable directions. Professor Jens Marklof has built a successful career understanding the mathematics that underpin the chaos of quantum systems.
His career, or indeed any academic career, is a kind of chaotic system. You never know which meeting or conversation will send you off in a new direction.
In a fascinating conversation, we explore key moments and opportunities in his career, like introducing himself to Peter Sarnak or sharing an office with David Thouless, shaped the scientist he is today.
Jens was the Rothschild Distinguished Visiting Fellow for the Isaac Newton Institute's programme on Geometric Spectral Theory (https://www.newton.ac.uk/event/gst/) . His public lecture, "The quantum centenary: from order to chaos (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_xzSeiGF0cY) " celebrated the 100th anniversary of quantum mechanics.
---

entry.title: Inside the 'Operators, Graphs, Groups' research programme

author.name: Isaac Newton Institute for Mathematical Sciences

media:group.media:title: Inside the 'Operators, Graphs, Groups' research programme
media:group.media:description:
This video features an exclusive interview with the esteemed Organisers of the 'Operators, Graphs, Groups' research programme. Join us as we sit down with Alex Lubotzky (Weizmann Institute of Science), Cornelia Drutu Badea (University of Oxford), and Alan Reid (Rice University).
In this discussion, they share their unique insights, reflections, and key highlights from the programme, which ran at the Institute from 7 July to 17 December 2025. Discover what made this research period particularly special and its broader impact on the field.
👉 For more information on the programme, you can visit: https://www.newton.ac.uk/event/ogg/
